content.text:
No, it isn't. `src/services/user-service.js` still imports `query` and `update` straight from `../db.js` and uses callbacks. The comment at `src/services/user-service.js:3` says so too: "Chapter 5 migrates this to UserRepository."

`UserRepository` in `src/repositories/user-repository.js` already has promise-based versions of all three functions:

| user-service.js (current) | UserRepository equivalent |
|---|---|
| `listActiveUsers(callback)` | `findActive()` |
| `findUser(id, callback)` | `findById(id)` |
| `softDeleteUser(id, when, callback)` | `softDelete(id, when)` |

The repository runs the same queries, so switching over mostly means changing the service from callbacks to promises. Anything that calls these functions, like `tests/user-service.test.js` and possibly `src/api/routes.js`, would need updating too. The project has a `migrate-module` skill that may cover this; I can run it if you'd like.
